text:
Dubai registered 11,608 residential sales valued at AED 34.33bn over the last four weeks, representing an 11.4 percent increase in volume and a 25.6 percent rise in value compared to the prior period. Mortgage registrations totaled 4,630, which are recorded separately from sales transactions. The market remains heavily weighted toward off-plan inventory, which accounted for 57.2 percent of all sales. Top performing areas by volume include Dubai South with 3,678 sales and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,295 sales over the last twelve weeks.

The median residential price stood at AED 1,688 per square foot, up 0.8 percent from the previous four-week average. Business Bay showed a 5.0 percent decline in median price per square foot over twelve weeks, while Majan recorded a 2.1 percent increase. Among top projects, RAW DISTRICT 2 BY IMTIAZ led with 559 sales at a median of AED 1,830 per square foot. Valia in Dubai Creek Harbour recorded 426 sales with a median price of AED 2,589 per square foot.

Rental activity remained robust with 91,552 Ejari contracts registered, where 51.3 percent were renewals. The median annual residential rent was AED 69,750. Estimated gross yields vary significantly by community, with Zaabeel First leading at 8.9 percent for flats. International City Phase 1 followed at 8.6 percent, while Town Square and Dubai Sports City recorded yields of 6.9 percent and 6.7 percent respectively.

The watch list highlights Al Yufrah 1 with a 43.3 percent twelve-week price increase and Dubai Industrial City at 12.8 percent. Conversely, Liwan and Palm Deira cooled with price declines of 13.3 percent and 13.0 percent. An anomaly monitor flagged 1,037 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from comparable medians. These figures are based on registered DLD data and medians, excluding bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
